title: Research
text:
Working Papers
The Political Economy of Resource Booms With Maria Coauthor. Revise and Resubmit, Quarterly Journal of Economics. [PDF] [Slides]

Resource booms reshape the political incentives of incumbent governments. We use newly digitized data on mineral discoveries from 1960–2010 to show that windfalls increase incumbency advantage by 12 percentage points, with effects concentrated in autocratic regimes.

Migration, Remittances, and Local Labor Markets With Pat Coauthor and Sam Coauthor. Submitted. [PDF] [Appendix]

We study the local labor market effects of large-scale outmigration using a shift-share design exploiting destination-country shocks. A 10% emigration shock raises local wages by 2.4% on average.

Information, Voting, and Accountability With Lee Researcher. [PDF]

A field experiment in collaboration with a national audit office tests whether disclosing local government performance scorecards changes voter behavior. We find significant effects on turnout but mixed effects on incumbent vote share.
